title: Cost-per-use thinking
description: A $90 item used 90 times can be better value than a $20 item used twice.

body.heading: Divide by the uses
paragraphs: Cost-per-use is simple: price divided by how many times you will realistically use something. Shoes worn daily for a year cost pennies per wear; a novelty gadget used twice can be expensive per use even if it was cheap.
This way of thinking often favours buying fewer, better things you will use constantly — and skipping cheap things you will barely touch.

body.heading: Be honest about 'will use'
paragraphs: The trick is honesty. A gym kit only has a low cost per use if you actually go. If you are unsure, borrow, rent, or buy second-hand first and see whether the habit sticks.
Quality matters most for things you use daily and that affect comfort or safety. For rare occasions, the cheapest reasonable option often wins.

body.heading: Value is personal
paragraphs: Cost-per-use is a lens, not a rule. A special item used rarely but loved deeply can still be worth it to you. The point is choosing with your eyes open.

takeaway: Judge value by cost per use, not just the price tag.
